sources.title: University of St Andrews / University of Stirling AHRC Corpus of Scottish Medieval Parish Churches: Dundee Parish Church
sources.institution: University of St Andrews and University of Stirling
sources.finding: After December 1547 Dundee English occupation, commander Thomas Wyndham letter dated 12 January 1548 records St Mary's steeple artillery and 20 men; English retreat later January with bells, copper and brass removed and steeple fired. Burgh record 1551 confirms English bell plunder. Historic church site NGR NO 40186 30136 (not burned-area boundary).
sources.read_scope: Historical outline and numbered notes 34–39 read; cited contemporary letter and Dundee burgh records not physically inspected
sources.precision_warning: The historic church reference point is usable as a targeted site, not a proxy for whole Dundee English controlled polygon.
sources.publisher: University of St Andrews and University of Stirling

sources.title: Stephen T. Driscoll, Excavations on Dundee Law, 1993, Proceedings of the Society of Antiquaries of Scotland 125 (1995), 1091–1108
sources.institution: Society of Antiquaries of Scotland / Glasgow University repository
sources.finding: Historical section printed pp.1105–1107: Dundee English seizure late 1547 followed by Argyll relief January 1548; Balgillo Hill fort constructed early 1548, August 1548 English siege and second occupation of Dundee with town burning; long-term control end after August not established in excerpt. Dundee Law earthwork Tudor date hypothesized, not archaeologically proven.
sources.read_scope: Full research paper historical section consulted via archaeologydataservice hosted PDF; source itself relies partly on historical syntheses and state paper citations
sources.precision_warning: Do not paint all modern Dundee as year-end English occupied in 1548. Dundee Law old earthworks lack unequivocal Tudor dating.
sources.publisher: Society of Antiquaries of Scotland / Glasgow University repository

sources.title: Historic Environment Scotland, Hailes Castle: Statement of Significance (last reviewed 2012; © 2019)
sources.finding: Historical Overview printed p.2/7 (PDF physical p.4): 1548 Lord Grey of Wilton captures Hailes for England; Scots soon recapture the castle within that same year and reportedly move its great iron gates to Edinburgh. Regent Arran orders Lord Borthwick to guard against the English. This contradicts research assumptions that Hailes English garrison was demonstrably still active at 1548 year-end, or uncertain in 1549. Day/month unverified by this institutional source.
sources.read_scope: Official public PDF historical timeline directly inspected and visual screenshot page 3 (zero-index) checked; original correspondence not individually opened.
sources.precision_warning: Source gives 1548 same-year recapture, not exact August date; later physical castle walls may not be Tudor 1548 fort lines. Official publication text under Open Government Licence v3.0 excluding images/logos, but GIS survey redrawing still not authorized by this finding.
